join_order.notes: Resolve single int32 target_ct_id by scanning kind.off/kind.dat once; then mc passes iff mc_ct[r] == target_ct_id.
title is dense PK driver; for each surviving t_id walk mc_off[t_id]..mc_off[t_id+1] using offsets_only index.
After mc filters survive (small), probe mi_off[t_id]..mi_off[t_id+1] for each surviving t_id; emit rows where mi.info IN set.
info_type has no filter and is dense PK 0..112; every mi.info_type_id is guaranteed to match. Join is a no-op and can be omitted at runtime.

data_structures.title_year_filter: streamed (no materialization; evaluated inline per morsel)
data_structures.mi_info_set: small inline switch on length then memcmp against 10 literals (length-bucketed); ~10 literals all short -> branchy compare faster than hash
data_structures.aggregation: per-thread local min char buffer + final reduce; single scalar MIN(title)

parallelism.morsel: title row ranges of 65536 t_ids; each worker keeps local best_title (string) and final reducer picks lexicographic min

notes_for_codegen: Resolve target_ct_id ONCE before parallel region by scanning company_type/kind.off+kind.dat (4 entries).
Skip info_type entirely: dense PK, no filter -> every mi.info_type_id matches.

Per-title pipeline: (1) year filter on title; (2) if pass, iterate mc range, apply ct + note filters; (3) if any mc row passes, iterate mi range, apply info IN; (4) on first surviving (mc,mi) combination per t_id, read title and update local min (early-exit inner loops since MIN cares only about existence of any surviving combo for that t_id).
Once title is admitted to MIN candidate set, we still need to compare lexicographically against current best; but inner loops over mc/mi can break on first match for that t_id.
varlen comparisons: keep best as owned std::string per thread; compare new title via lexicographic compare on (ptr,len).
Length prefilter mc.note: len>=5 before memmem; mi.info: bucket by length (3,5,6,7,8) before memcmp.
